references_named: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: The mechanism is the argument: a near-threshold tinted-black cross rendered live on a backlit surface Reinhardt forbade, with a JPEG round-trip that performs reproduction-as-erasure on demand. Concept and execution collapse into one object (P1) — the canvas quantization literally enacts Benjamin's aura-loss and Reinhardt's anti-reproduction dogma. Double-coding is strong (P7): a black rectangle and a button for the casual viewer; Reinhardt/Malevich/Benjamin triangulation for the literate one. Restraint is exemplary (P3): no animation, no persistence, no network, the smallest build that completes the thought.
reservations: The 'Make a reproduction' button is a slightly literal device — it announces the gag rather than letting it ambush. A subtler version might trigger the JPEG round-trip on a less obvious gesture (e.g., a screenshot attempt, a visibility change, or simply on first interaction) so the erasure feels like the medium's reflex rather than a labeled button. Minor: the wall-label text is a touch long for the 'no wall text' ideal, though it stays in the dark-room register.
revision_suggestion: Consider removing or renaming the explicit button so the reproduction-as-erasure happens as an ambient consequence of the medium (e.g., on visibilitychange, on a screenshot key, or via a right-click context menu) — letting the web's reflex perform the erasure rather than asking the viewer to press 'Make a reproduction.' Tighten the label to one or two lines.
